text:
Other way around.  Competitive games you don't want it on.  You can't interact with the fake frames anyway so you have to wait for the real frames in order to make inputs.  Plus if you have fast randomized motion like in a shooter it's prone to creating graphical artifacts .    

The time it takes for the card to generate the interpolated frames also increases the input lag.

What it IS good at is allowing you to run very high settings on single player cinematic titles and still get great motion clarity.

A game you can normally only run at say medium settings you can now crank all the way to high or ultra and frame gen will still give you more frames than you started with.

The slight bit of extra input lag doesn't matter in single player games and the extra smooth motion with better graphics really helps single player titles.
